title: Memory Candidate
description: One item proposed for long-term memory, extracted after the interview rather than during it. Two rules are structural. A memory cannot exist without its reason: why_it_earns_preservation is required and non-empty, so a note that cannot say why it matters cannot be stored. And a memory cannot exist without evidence: supported_by must reference at least one fact from the entry. Third-party privacy is enforced by the shape of person_ref, which holds a single given name and a generic relation category and nothing else. There is deliberately no field anywhere in this file for a surname, an employer, an address, a phone number, an email, a handle, a profile link or a photo, and additionalProperties is false at every level, so no writer can add one. A place is a label that cannot contain digits, so a street number or a postcode cannot be written into it.

entry_id.description: The journal entry this was extracted from

statement.description: The memory itself, in the user's own words where possible

why_it_earns_preservation.description: Why the user would be worse off in three months without this. Mandatory: a memory whose reason cannot be written is a note, not a memory.

supported_by.description: Fact ids from the entry. At least one, so a memory can never rest on an impression alone.

durability.description: durable is expected to still matter in a year. provisional is re-read at the weekly rollup and discarded if it has gone flat.

occurrences.description: Incremented instead of storing a duplicate. A third occurrence is pattern input for the contradiction engine.

discard_reason.description: Required on a discard. Recording the discard is cheaper than the later doubt about whether it was ever there.

user_vetoed.description: The user struck it. A vetoed candidate is deleted rather than archived, and this flag exists only so the deletion can be logged.

allOf.description: A new person is stored with the given name and, in the statement, why they may matter. Without the person_ref the entry is an anecdote.
A relationship development names which relationship changed.
A meaningful place carries its label.
A recurring pattern has been seen more than once, by definition.

kind.description: The closed list of what earns long-term memory. Trivia merely mentioned has no kind and therefore cannot be stored.

person_ref.description: The ONLY permitted representation of a third party. They did not consent to be in this file, so the structure holds a given name and a generic relation category at most.

first_name.description: A single given name or an initial. The pattern rejects whitespace, digits and punctuation, so a full name, an email, a handle or an address cannot be written here.

relation.description: A generic category. There is no free-text description field, because a description is how an identity gets written down.

label.description: A generic label such as the river path or the corner cafe. Digits are rejected, so a street number, a postcode or a door code cannot be written here.
